title: Keeping Comparable Company Sets Current
answer: Keeping comparable company sets current is the work of maintaining a peer group used for valuation, benchmarking, and relative performance analysis as companies change. In finance agent workflows, this means an agent watches for events that alter comparability, such as mergers, acquisitions, spin-offs, delistings, sector reclassifications, and shifts in business mix. The scope covers defining the peer criteria, monitoring the universe, and deciding when a set needs revision. The site's 432 company pages are one example of a structured universe an agent could track.

sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: The workflow runs on scheduled data pipelines that pull daily prices, corporate actions, and filings into a store that agents can query. The site's 117 listed AI-related instruments with daily prices illustrate the kind of price feed that keeps a comp set fresh. Agents typically run on a job orchestrator, use a relational or vector database for reference data, and call language models to read unstructured text. Human analysts review proposed changes through a dashboard or ticketing system.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: The method starts with a written peer definition, then an agent ingests new filings, news, and financial statements to detect events that break comparability. The site's 354 merger and acquisition filings are a primary signal for comparability breaks. The agent scores each event for materiality, proposes additions or removals, and records the reason and source for every change. A human approves or rejects the proposal, and the approved set is versioned with an effective date. Backtests compare the updated set against the prior one to check that the change improves the analysis.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Governance covers data rights, audit trails, and the provenance of every input that drives a change. Each proposed update carries its source, timestamp, and the rule or model that produced it, so an analyst can trace why a company entered or left the set. Risk includes stale data, misread filings, and unintended bias in peer selection, all of which can distort valuations. The site's 219 compliance and regulation pages reflect the kind of oversight material that may constrain how agents handle sensitive data.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: The direction is toward continuous, event-driven comp sets that update within minutes of a filing rather than on a quarterly cycle. Agents will likely coordinate with valuation models and portfolio systems, proposing changes that a human signs off on. As the number of listed AI-related instruments grows, the manual effort to keep peer groups current will push more firms to adopt agent workflows. The direction points to tighter integration with audit and compliance tooling, and more emphasis on explainable change logs.
